decisions.reason: This multisite Registered Report re-tests three statistical findings from Soto et al. (2011): (1) above-chance working memory (WM) performance on unseen cue-present trials, (2) a non-significant correlation between cue detection sensitivity and WM performance, and (3) an above-chance regression intercept of WM performance on sensitivity. While the authors replicate the above-chance WM performance in unseen trials (Hypothesis 1) and the positive regression intercept (Hypothesis 3), they explicitly state that they did not reproduce Soto et al.'s null correlation (Hypothesis 2), finding a significant positive correlation instead (r = .228, p < .001 vs. Soto et al.'s r = -.18, p = .41). Under the codebook, where the authors confirm the primary tested effect as one comparison but explicitly mark another tested finding as differing from the original without a superseding whole-replication verdict, the replication outcome is 'mixed'. Both shipped and blind codings correctly recorded 'mixed' (though the prior blind quote omitted intervening text between lines 377 and 397, which is preserved contiguously here).
